channel.title: MAKE / BREAK
channel.description: Put the phone down. Go make the machine misbehave. A free zine every other week: security in plain English, a beginner's tip, and one thing to build or break. By the Norfolk Hacker.

item.title: Issue #06 — Boot your own OS
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a two-minute check on what your phone's apps can reach, and the project: boot acid OS, a tiny operating system, and bring the #00 plasma back to life as one of its apps.

item.title: Issue #05 — Sniff the air
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a beginner's fix for the trail your phone leaves, and the project: turn a £4 ESP32 into a Wi-Fi sniffer and hear what your own devices are shouting into the room.

item.title: Issue #04 — Make it confess
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a beginner's superpower for spotting dodgy files, and the project: write a program that guards a password, then defeat it without ever running it.

item.title: Issue #03 — Make Pure Data scream
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a 30-second check to see if you've already been breached, and the project: a little machine that plays music and never repeats itself.

item.title: Issue #02 — Recon that isn't a checklist
item.description: This week's security in plain English, the account upgrade that kills most phishing dead, and the project: how real bug-hunting starts — by looking, not by running ten tools.

item.title: Issue #01 — Fold the light
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a two-minute fix that stops the most common way people get hacked, and a build: turn last issue's plasma into a living kaleidoscope.

item.title: Issue #00 — The one where you start
item.description: This week's security in plain English, a beginner's tip that beats any antivirus, and a build: a plasma you make and break live on the page.
